records.Name: Drop in 4/29/26
records.MeetingNotes:
Ct arrived to drop in in a quiet mood. Inquired about mail she was expecting and when we checked the mailbox her SS check was there. Ct was excited, as evidenced by jumping for joy and screaming excitedly. Ct wanted to go to King Soopers to cash the check but due to her not having a real ID yet, she was unable to do so. Ct returned to center visably upset, as evidenced by slumped shoulders, not engaging in conversation. Ct purchased snacks from the Circle K and took a nap on the couch.

ADDENDUM: CM Cate drove client to attempt to cash her social security checks. Enroute we discussed the very real possibility of client being unable to accomplish this, as she only had a paper copy from the DMV. Preferred not call in advance. After King Soopers we drove to Chase bank. Client was educated in the life skill of opening a bank account & was observed interacting with the bank staff by asking questions. Was advised that she would need to return with her real state ID or passport-cb.

records.Name: Drop in 5/5/26
records.MeetingNotes: Ct arrived early to drop-in and requested to check the mail as she is still awaiting receipt of her real ID. Ct spent the morning watching Disney movies and remained mostly to herself. During the shift, while her phone was charging, her phone began ringing loudly which was disruptive to others in the space. Ct was asked to answer her phone or to mute it, which she did not want to do. Another staff member got up and muted her phone, which upset the Ct and she expressed not wanting anyone to touch her phone. Ct began speaking negatively about the staff who had touched her phone and was becoming agitated. When staff attempted to set a boundary with her about muting the phone and not speaking negatively about the staff, Ct was unreceptive. Later in the day, Ct was feeling sad about her interactions earlier, as evidenced by tears and dialog around not feeling wanted anywhere. Staff and CM assured Ct that she was welcome and wanted in the space. Ct continued to watch movies for the remained of the day and was able to communicate how she was feeling. Ongoing communication will be attempted with Ct to set appropriate boundaries around what is appropriate to say while she is in the space.

records.Name: Ward, Sasha - 05/06/2026 - Maggie Reed
records.MeetingNotes: Ct arrived to drop in to celebrate her birthday.  Ct was anxious to check the mail in anticipation of her ID being delivered, which it was not.  Ct enjoyed her birthday cake and was able to enjoy a meal with us in the early afternoon.  Ct became more agitated as the afternoon progressed and requested to speak with YSS (Maggie) privately.  During this discussion we set the boundary again about being respectful of staff and respecting the space.  Ct expressed increased concerns about an individual making threats against her and reported being followed by an unknown individual.  Ct expressed concerns for her safety, and the safety of others and it was determined that a police report would be necessary.  Ct and YSS made a report via the police non-emergency line and continued ongoing safety planning.  Ct is planning to go to All Roads for overnight shelter and will return to The Source in the morning.

records.Name: Drop In  5/12/26
records.MeetingNotes: Ct arrived to the drop in center in a mental daze, as evidenced by eyes glazed over, not engaging in conversation, seemed very distracted. Ct disclosed a few diagnoses to staff, including schizophrenia and PTSD. Ct was experiencing heavy auditory hallucinations and having conversations to herself. Staff was able to complete a basic intake, as Ct requested a case manager and expressed the desire to get an updated ID with her preferred name and gender markers. Had a brief discussion with Ct about getting her connected to Rocky Mountain Equality. Ct was not in a state to have coherent conversations so staff decided not to engaged in any goal setting or further case management until Ct was in a more coherent state of mind.
